AEC Tech Hackathon · New York · November 2026

Roomboard

The problem

Everyone has stood in a room that felt right.
Ask why, and everyone answers differently.

timeless cozy not too big human scale light-filled elegant feels expensive feels right “like that café we went to” tiny, but airy warm every inch works grand, not cold “like this photo” quiet

Owners and architects both talk in precedents. Images get sent back and forth. Sometimes they’re spot on, but often the room in the picture is far off from the size they have in mind, and from what actually fits the space they’re imagining. Nobody checks the numbers until the drawings do.

Thesis

A library of real, measured spaces becomes a shared language between people.

What one person imaginesWhat another understands

Close that gap. Owners, architects and contractors first, but really anyone who has ever tried to describe a room they loved.

Roomboard

A moodboard curates how a space feels.

Roomboard gives those feelings definition.

What gets lost

Inspiration, experiences and spaces are saved flat today.

Camera rolls, mood boards and pin boards keep the look and lose the room. A photo of a café can’t tell you it is 16 feet wide with a 12 foot ceiling, which is the whole reason it felt right.

PHASE 1

Capture & archive

Scan the spaces you love. Each becomes a measured record, sorted into categories with dimensions.

This weekend

Stitch

→
GeometryPHASE 3A

Fit

ExperiencePHASE 2B

ExperiencePHASE 3B

Specify

Turn the reimagined room into a finish schedule of real products, at three price points.

PHASE 2ANext · geometry track

Stitch

Arrange saved spaces into a plan. Rooms keep their size; corridors and thresholds absorb the mismatch. The result is the girth of a building before anyone draws it.

In
A set of rooms from your library
Out
A plan and massing with square footage and volume
PHASE 3ALater · geometry track

Fit

New build or existing building: drop a space from your library in and test it. Can the auditorium you once visited fit in the warehouse you just leased? Where does it conflict?

In
A library space plus a site or existing building
Out
A fit test with named conflicts: columns, clear height, egress
PHASE 2BNext · experience track

Reimagine

You love the scale of a room, not the room. Keep the walls, windows and ceiling height, and let generative AI rebuild it as something else entirely.

Same room, same dimensions, two different lives.

What Roomboard brings

Save the room.
Get the size, the fit and the price.

Roomboard turns the rooms people love into measured, shareable records. From there a feeling becomes a plan, a fit test and a budget, and everyone works from the same room.

OWNERS

Show, don’t describe

Point to rooms you have stood in. See them stitched into a plan with real square footage, or reimagined at the same size.

ARCHITECTS

Start from the real thing

Briefs arrive with dimensions and precedent. Test a saved room inside a real building and see the conflicts before drawing.

BUILDERS

Price it early

Area, volume and finishes are known up front, with real products at three price points for the same look.

EVERYONE

One shared language

The gap between what one person imagines and another understands shrinks, because the room itself is the reference.
